top.line: News history, checked: my memo was wrong four times
top.para: A voice memo on four eras of news, print, web, platforms and AI, was researched and corrected in four places. The reader has been the product since 1833, the web took the monopoly rather than the model, platforms made the reader measurable, and AI removed traffic. The unused 402 payment code marks the road not taken.

s0.line: Readers were always the product; only the owner changed
s0.para: The penny press made the reader the product in 1833, and advertising was 82% of US newspaper revenue by 2005. The web took the local monopoly, platforms took 54.7% of digital advertising by 2017, newsrooms lost 57% of jobs, and AI removed traffic. Circulation overtook advertising in 2021, while HTTP 402 has stayed reserved since 1997.

s1.line: Monopoly, not the advertising model, paid for journalism
s1.para: Before 1833 papers were subscription products; the penny press made advertising the revenue and the reader the audience sold. In 2005 advertising brought $49.4 billion against $10.7 billion from circulation. Journalism was funded by local monopolies earning 20 to 30 per cent, Buffett's unregulated toll bridge, whose owners chose to overinvest in reporting.

s2.line: The web removed the monopoly bridge, not the model
s2.para: Classifieds were about 40% of newspaper revenue, and Craigslist alone cost at least $5 billion between 2000 and 2007; classifieds fell from $19.6 billion in 2000 to about $6 billion in 2009. Display advertising lost its exclusivity too. The failure was not misunderstanding technology but not seeing that distribution had been the moat.

s3.line: Platforms made readers measurable and rewarded falsehood over truth
s3.para: Cookies and AdSense let Google and Meta take 54.7% of US digital advertising by 2017, and Facebook referrals fell 58% in six years. False news was 70% more likely to be retweeted, and Facebook weighted emoji reactions at five times a like. US newspaper newsrooms fell from about 71,000 jobs to 31,000, cutting provenance work.

s4.line: AI removed traffic, and the industry turned to rent
s4.para: Organic search traffic to publishers fell 33% in the year to November 2025, while crawlers fetched 38,000 pages per visitor Anthropic sent back. Fetching is wasteful on both sides. In 2021 US circulation revenue overtook advertising, $11.5 billion against $10.3 billion, but the industry sells subscriptions, which is rent rather than a return to 1832.

s5.line: Paying creators was reserved in HTTP in 1997, unused
s5.para: HTTP/1.1 reserved 402 Payment Required in 1997, and it remains unused. DigiCash went bankrupt in 1998, Szabo and Shirky argued against micropayments, and advertising became the default through small decisions such as banners, cookies, pop-ups and AdSense. iTunes sold a million songs in a week in 2003 and Substack passed five million paid subscriptions.

s6.line: Stop charging for the road; charge for the cargo
s6.para: The corrections point one way: no distribution-dependent model will fund journalism again, paying for attention pays for falsehood, and provenance returns only if it is what is paid for. So sell the story as a graph with hashed evidence, in pence, to readers, firms and agents, with money flowing back to whoever made the fact.

s7.line: Sources: the histories, studies and figures cited
s7.para: Sources include Pew Research Center revenue and newsroom figures, Nicholas Lemann in the New York Review of Books, Poynter on classifieds, Seamans and Zhu on Craigslist, Press Gazette and Chartbeat traffic data, the Vosoughi, Roy and Aral study, Cloudflare's crawl-to-click data, Szabo, Shirky, Zuckerman, Apple's iTunes releases and Substack's milestone.
